ASVS Requirement Description: Verify that data selection or database queries (e.g., SQL, HQL, NoSQL, Cypher) use parameterized queries, ORMs, entity frameworks, or are otherwise protected from SQL Injection and other database injection attacks. This is also relevant when writing stored procedures.
Application Component: Auth.js user lookup; Prisma admin entity repository
Reason for Selection: The credential lookup and admin entity search use request-derived values in PostgreSQL queries.
Testing Objective: Determine whether sampled lookup and list queries treat user input as data.
Testing Method: Inspect source and trace server inputs into the Prisma query calls.
Expected Secure Result: Sampled query values are handled through the ORM or explicit parameter binding.
Evidence Required: Input-to-query trace and versioned excerpts showing construction or binding.

ASVS Requirement Description: Verify that input is validated to enforce business or functional expectations for that input. This should either use positive validation against an allow list of values, patterns, and ranges, or be based on comparing the input to an expected structure and logical limits according to predefined rules. For L1, this can focus on input which is used to make specific business or security decisions. For L2 and up, this should apply to all input.
Application Component: Auth.js credentials; admin entity list and create validators
Reason for Selection: Sign-in and account management make security and business decisions from user-supplied fields.
Testing Objective: Verify the sampled fields conform to intended formats, bounds and allowlists.
Testing Method: Inspect rules and observe ordinary valid and invalid synthetic inputs.
Expected Secure Result: Valid inputs follow the intended rule set. Invalid inputs create neither a session nor an entity.
Evidence Required: Auditee rule table, source references, redacted paired observations and no-write evidence for the creation sample.

ASVS Requirement Description: Verify that the application is designed to enforce input validation at a trusted service layer. While client-side validation improves usability and should be encouraged, it must not be relied upon as a security control.
Application Component: Auth.js authorize; admin entity route; management service and Zod schemas
Reason for Selection: Browser input controls and the server both handle input used for identity and account creation.
Testing Objective: Locate and verify validation in the trusted server before session creation or writes.
Testing Method: Trace server-side validation and review an approved isolated validation check.
Expected Secure Result: Server-side checks reject invalid input before any protected state change.
Evidence Required: Handler-to-validator trace and independent server-side rejection evidence with no session or write.

ASVS Requirement Description: Verify that HTTP requests to sensitive functionality use appropriate HTTP methods such as POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE, and not methods defined by the HTTP specification as "safe" such as HEAD, OPTIONS, or GET. Alternatively, strict validation of the Sec-Fetch-* request header fields can be used to ensure that the request did not originate from an inappropriate cross-origin call, a navigation request, or a resource load (such as an image source) where this is not expected.
Application Component: Auth.js sign-in and sign-out; admin entities GET and POST
Reason for Selection: The local lab provides browser-accessible operations that authenticate users, end sessions and create entities.
Testing Objective: Verify sensitive operations use appropriate methods and safe methods preserve state.
Testing Method: Inspect method routing and observe ordinary interaction metadata; use existing mutation evidence.
Expected Secure Result: Sensitive actions use appropriate state-changing methods or an evidenced ASVS-permitted alternative; safe navigation does not trigger them.
Evidence Required: Operation/method map, handler references, redacted observations and safe-method state evidence.

ASVS Requirement Description: Verify that application documentation defines how controls such as rate limiting, anti-automation, and adaptive response, are used to defend against attacks such as credential stuffing and password brute force. The documentation must make clear how these controls are configured and prevent malicious account lockout.
Application Component: Security documentation for Auth.js sign-in and rate limiting
Reason for Selection: Happy Town accepts passwords and includes a sign-in abuse-control path that needs operating documentation.
Testing Objective: Check whether documentation describes credential-abuse defenses, settings and account lockout prevention.
Testing Method: Inspect controlled documentation and confirm the design with the auditee.
Expected Secure Result: The documented protection, configuration and lockout-abuse safeguards are clear.
Evidence Required: Controlled document references and corroborated auditee notes, including status of missing material.

ASVS Requirement Description: Verify that password input fields use type=password to mask the entry. Applications may allow the user to temporarily view the entire masked password, or the last typed character of the password.
Reason for Selection: The credentials form accepts a password and offers an optional reveal control.
Testing Objective: Verify that a password is masked by default and reveal requires user action.
Testing Method: Inspect the form source and observe the rendered field in a clean browser.
Expected Secure Result: The field defaults to type=password and can be remasked after intentional reveal.
Evidence Required: Versioned source and redacted DOM evidence or screenshots showing default and restored masking.

ASVS Requirement Description: Verify that controls to prevent attacks such as credential stuffing and password brute force are implemented according to the application's security documentation.
Application Component: Auth.js credential handler; login rate limiter
Reason for Selection: The credential handler and limiter are the app's implementation points for the documented login defenses.
Testing Objective: Compare implemented credential-abuse defenses to the documented baseline.
Testing Method: Trace the sign-in flow, review the isolated limiter run and run the audited Credentials provider with in-memory dependencies. Observe public login reachability separately.
Expected Secure Result: Configured defenses operate as documented for the sampled topology.
Evidence Required: Documentation-to-code comparison and authorized isolated results covering documented behaviors, with sanitized audit events as corroboration.
21 Nov Follow-up: Fail on source/configuration comparison against approved baseline. Live lockout and recovery unobserved.

ASVS Requirement Description: Verify that default user accounts (e.g., "root", "admin", or "sa") are not present in the application or are disabled.
Application Component: Prisma seed and bootstrap; synthetic user inventory
Reason for Selection: Bootstrap and lab seeding can create active application accounts, including privileged users.
Testing Objective: Determine whether enabled default accounts are present.
Testing Method: Inspect account setup paths and reconcile an authorized sanitized inventory.
Expected Secure Result: Default accounts are absent or disabled; active seed logins require explicit operator-supplied credentials.
Evidence Required: Versioned seed/bootstrap excerpts and sanitized role/status inventory with provisioning reconciliation.

ASVS Requirement Description: Verify that the application performs all session token verification using a trusted, backend service.
Application Component: Auth.js auth(); server guards; sampled protected routes
Reason for Selection: Protected backend paths use session identity to determine whether a request can proceed.
Testing Objective: Verify the trusted backend validates the session token before using its identity.
Testing Method: Trace session verification and compare ordinary authenticated and signed-out observations.
Expected Secure Result: The backend validates the session token and signed-out requests receive no protected data.
Evidence Required: Backend call chain, versioned Auth.js reference and redacted paired role and response observations.

ASVS Requirement Description: Verify that the application uses either self-contained or reference tokens that are dynamically generated for session management, i.e. not using static API secrets and keys.
Reason for Selection: Auth.js issues a self-contained application session token after credential authentication.
Testing Objective: Verify the session token is dynamically issued and is not a fixed application credential.
Testing Method: Inspect issuance design and compare two normal sign-ins using redacted issuance metadata.
Expected Secure Result: Independent sign-ins receive dynamically generated session tokens.
Evidence Required: Versioned strategy and issuance references plus a comparison result without token values.

ASVS Requirement Description: Verify that the application generates a new session token on user authentication, including re-authentication, and terminates the current session token.
Reason for Selection: JWT-backed sessions make both new issuance and invalidation of a superseded session relevant.
Testing Objective: Determine whether authentication and re-authentication issue fresh tokens and terminate the superseded session.
Testing Method: Review supported transitions and authorized isolated lifecycle evidence; observe ordinary issuance.
Expected Secure Result: The new token is fresh and the replaced session is unusable.
Evidence Required: Transition inventory, redacted issuance comparison and corroborated evidence of backend invalidation.
21 Nov Follow-up: A retained access after B signed in as the same account. Source Fail. Exact superseded credential acceptance unobserved.

ASVS Requirement Description: Verify that when session termination is triggered (such as logout or expiration), the application disallows any further use of the session. For reference tokens or stateful sessions, this means invalidating the session data at the application backend. Applications using self-contained tokens will need a solution such as maintaining a list of terminated tokens, disallowing tokens produced before a per-user date and time or rotating a per-user signing key.
Application Component: Auth.js sign-out; expiration; protected backend routes
Reason for Selection: All roles use the shared session lifecycle and access sensitive information while signed in.
Testing Objective: Determine whether logout and expiration prevent further use of the terminated session at the backend.
Testing Method: Observe ordinary sign-out and review backend lifecycle design and isolated evidence.
Expected Secure Result: After logout or expiry the terminated session can no longer access protected functionality.
Evidence Required: Before/after access observations and backend evidence for termination and expiration enforcement.
21 Nov Follow-up: Ordinary logout confirmed. Source Fail stands. Earlier-session acceptance after logout unobserved.

ASVS Requirement Description: Verify that authorization documentation defines rules for restricting function-level and data-specific access based on consumer permissions and resource attributes.
Application Component: Role documentation; parent/student and teacher/group relationships
Reason for Selection: Human-readable access rules are needed for the distinct role and record permissions in the sample.
Testing Objective: Verify that the auditee documents function access and record permissions.
Testing Method: Inspect authorization documentation and confirm the intended rules with the auditee.
Expected Secure Result: Current documentation defines access by role, function and relevant resource attributes.
Evidence Required: Versioned authorization documentation and confirmed notes on exceptions or gaps.

ASVS Requirement Description: Verify that the application ensures that function-level access is restricted to consumers with explicit permissions.
Application Component: ADMIN, TEACHER and PARENT portals; admin entities API
Reason for Selection: The application exposes distinct functions and an administrator-only management surface.
Testing Objective: Verify that sampled functions are accessible only to roles with explicit permission.
Testing Method: Compare positive and negative read-only role fixtures and corroborate backend enforcement.
Expected Secure Result: Permitted roles can use the sampled function; denied roles and anonymous cases receive no protected content.
Evidence Required: Redacted role-by-function observations with statuses or navigation outcomes and protected-data assertions.

ASVS Requirement Description: Verify that the application ensures that data-specific access is restricted to consumers with explicit permissions to specific data items to mitigate insecure direct object reference (IDOR) and broken object level authorization (BOLA).
Application Component: Student and group reads; parent and teacher relationship guards
Reason for Selection: Student and group permissions depend on ownership relationships in addition to role.
Testing Objective: Verify access follows the approved student/group relationships and role rules.
Testing Method: Compare paired approved record fixtures with linked and unlinked relationships.
Expected Secure Result: Only explicitly allowed records and associated protected data are returned.
Evidence Required: Redacted fixture relationship record and paired allow/deny observations including data presence.

ASVS Requirement Description: Verify that the application enforces authorization rules at a trusted service layer and doesn't rely on controls that an untrusted consumer could manipulate, such as client-side JavaScript.
Application Component: Server-side page and API guards; management service; ownership queries
Reason for Selection: A role-aware UI exists alongside backend pages, route handlers and data-access paths.
Testing Objective: Verify backend authorization gates the actions and data independently of client UI.
Testing Method: Trace identity and enforcement through server entry points and corroborate approved backend observations.
Expected Secure Result: Trusted server-side checks enforce permissions before returning data or making protected changes.
Evidence Required: Versioned route-to-guard-to-data trace and linked approved role and record fixture observations.

ASVS Requirement Description: Verify that sensitive data is only sent to the server in the HTTP message body or header fields, and that the URL and query string do not contain sensitive information, such as an API key or session token.
Application Component: Credentials, session and sampled role requests
Reason for Selection: Sign-in and authenticated requests carry sensitive identifiers, credentials or session material.
Testing Objective: Determine whether sampled sensitive request values stay in bodies or headers and out of URLs.
Testing Method: Inspect request-building code and review sanitized metadata from normal flows.
Expected Secure Result: Sampled URLs and query strings contain no sensitive values under the agreed classification.
Evidence Required: Redacted request-location worksheet with field locations and versioned routing or client references.
